text: Research · Data as of November 6, 2026 We looked at 178,637 apps that appeared in the App Store top charts of 173 countries and regions since October 9, 2026. Here are the answers to five questions. Download all figures (CSV) 17,456 apps (9.8%) mention AI, GPT, machine learning, generative or chatbot in their name or the start of their description. They cluster in Graphics & Design, Photo & Video and Developer Tools. Ratings barely differ: among apps with at least 50 ratings, those mentioning AI average 4.49 stars and the rest 4.4. Of 164,056 free-to-download apps, 26.7% say in their description that they offer in-app purchases, a subscription, a trial or a Pro unlock. Graphics & Design and Photo & Video lead; Shopping and News come last; many of those are apps of businesses that most likely earn their money outside the app. By our definition (see the notes below), 67.3% of apps in the charts come from independent developers. Their ratings match the larger publishers': 4.41 against 4.41 stars for apps with at least 50 ratings. The share is highest in Developer Tools, Sports and Navigation and lowest in Games. 70.9% of apps in the charts were updated in the last six months, yet 20.3% have gone a year or more without an update and 9.8% more than three years. Books, Reference and News have the most apps left alone; Finance the fewest (10.9%). We read 165,735 US App Store reviews of 3,912 apps. Among 1-2 star reviews, 12.7% complain about subscription & price, 10.9% about bugs & broken features and 10% about login & account. One review can fall under several themes. We will refresh this report every quarter. From the next edition it will show change over time: which apps moved to subscriptions, how fast the AI share grows, and whether abandoned apps come back.
